pass_a_gloss: If we have crossed over out of the death into the life through having crossed over from unbelief into faith, let us not wonder if the world hates us. For no one who has not crossed over out of the death into the life but is remaining in the death is able to love those who have crossed over from the dark house (if I may name it so) of the death onto the buildings, filled with light of life, out of living stones. On behalf of us Jesus placed his soul, and we therefore let us also place it, I will not say on his behalf, but on our own behalf, and I suppose also on behalf of those who will be built up in our martyrdom. There has come upon us Christians a season of boastings; for not only, he says, but also boasting in the tribulations, having known that the tribulation works out endurance, and the endurance testedness, and the testedness hope; and the hope does not shame; only let the love of God have been poured out in our hearts through Holy Spirit. Let Paul indeed say: if according to man I beast-fought in Ephesus; but we: if according to man, I was taken off in Germany.
pass_b_english: If we have passed “from death to life” (1 John 3:14) by passing from unbelief to faith, let us not be surprised if the world hates us (1 John 3:13). For no one who has not passed “from death to life”, but remains in death, can love those who have moved out of the dark house of death, if I may call it that, into the buildings made of living stones (1 Peter 2:5) and filled with the light of life. Jesus “laid down his life for us” (1 John 3:16); let us, then, lay down ours as well. I will not say for his sake, but for our own, and also, I think, for those who will be built up by our martyrdom.

A time for boasting has come upon us Christians. For, he says, “not only so, but we also boast in our afflictions, knowing that affliction produces endurance, and endurance proven character, and proven character hope; and hope does not put us to shame” (Romans 5:3-5). Only let “the love of God” be poured out “in our hearts through the Holy Spirit” (Romans 5:5). Let Paul say, “If, humanly speaking, I fought with wild beasts at Ephesus” (1 Corinthians 15:32); and let us say, “If, humanly speaking, I was put to death in Germany.”

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 41); the old English was a digest: it opened with 1 John 3:16 and Romans 5, dropped the passage from death to life, the world's hatred and the house of living stones, and printed '(?)' marks in the Germany line.

Translated as printed: 'let us say, “If, humanly speaking, I was put to death in Germany.”' The verb 'say' is supplied from the preceding 'λεγέτω' (ellipsis in the Greek, not an unreadable word); no question marks in the reading text; crux recorded in translator_notes.
'Havuasomuev' read as 'θαυμάζωμεν' ('let us not be surprised'); 'pro' as 'φησι' ('he says'); 'oluaı' as 'οἶμαι'; 'καυχήσεῶν' as 'καυχήσεων'.
'life' in 1 John 3:16 and in 'lay down ours', since the idiom is laying down one's life.

Παῦλος μὲν λεγέτω" „el χατὰ ἄνϑρωπον ἐθηριομάχησα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ“, ἡμεῖς de „el χατὰ ἄνϑρωπον" ἀνῃρέϑην ἐν Γερμανίᾳ.
